nodes.name: ApiPaths
nodes.summary: Every path prefix, named once for the controllers and the security rules alike.

endpoints.summary: Creates the account unconfirmed and emails a code; the session comes with the code.
Confirms the email with the code from the letter and opens the first session.
Sends a new confirmation letter, at most once per cooldown.
Opens a session by email or username and password; an unconfirmed email gets a code instead.
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token and the next refresh token.
Revokes the session the refresh token belongs to; open, since the access token may have expired.
Whether a username is still free, for the sign-up form's live hint.
The signed-in user's saved picks; all fields null before the first save.
Saves the whole set of picks.

nodes.name: AppMailProperties
nodes.summary: Our own mail settings; the SMTP server itself is Spring Boot's `spring.mail.*`.

nodes.name: AsyncConfig
nodes.summary: `@Async` work (sending letters) runs on Spring Boot's task executor, so a slow SMTP server never holds up an HTTP response.

nodes.name: EmailTemplateProperties
nodes.summary: Where the letter templates are and what they are called.

nodes.name: JwtConfig
nodes.summary: The key access tokens are signed and checked with (HS256), and the encoder and decoder built on it.

nodes.name: JwtProperties
nodes.summary: Access tokens are short-lived JWTs; refresh tokens are opaque and live in the database.

nodes.name: MailConfig
nodes.summary: Our mail settings: the sender, the support address, where the letter templates are.

nodes.name: MapStructConfig
nodes.summary: Shared settings for every mapper: each one is a Spring bean, receives its collaborators through the constructor, and has its generated implementation in an impl package beside it.

nodes.name: SecurityConfig
nodes.summary: Stateless JWT security: no session, no CSRF token (nothing rides on a cookie), every request outside the open auth endpoints needs a valid Bearer access token.

nodes.name: VerificationProperties
nodes.summary: How one-time email codes behave.

nodes.name: AccentColor
nodes.summary: The eight interface accents.

nodes.name: Language
nodes.summary: The languages the app speaks: the interface language a user picks and the language letters are written in.

nodes.name: ThemeMode
nodes.summary: Dark or light interface.

nodes.name: LoginRequest
nodes.summary: Log in with an email or a username.

nodes.name: RefreshRequest
nodes.summary: Body of refresh and log out: the refresh token the client holds.

nodes.name: RegisterRequest
nodes.summary: Sign-up.

nodes.name: ResendCodeRequest
nodes.summary: Asks for a new confirmation letter.

nodes.name: VerifyEmailRequest
nodes.summary: The code from the confirmation letter, for the email it was sent to.

nodes.name: CodeAttemptsResponse
nodes.summary: The data of an "auth.codeInvalid" refusal: wrong guesses still allowed for this code.

nodes.name: RegistrationResponse
nodes.summary: Sign-up accepted: the account waits for its email to be confirmed, and a letter with the code is on its way to email.

nodes.name: RetryAfterResponse
nodes.summary: The data of an "auth.resendTooSoon" refusal: seconds until another letter may be asked for.

nodes.name: SessionResponse
nodes.summary: What log in, sign up and refresh answer with (client type `Session`).

nodes.name: UnconfirmedEmailResponse
nodes.summary: The data of an "auth.emailNotVerified" refusal at log in: the right password, an email not yet confirmed.

nodes.name: UserResponse
nodes.summary: The user as the client sees them (client type `User`).

nodes.name: ApiResponse
nodes.summary: The one shape every endpoint answers with, success or failure alike.

nodes.name: UpdateSettingsRequest
nodes.summary: Every pick at once: the client always sends the whole set it shows.

nodes.name: SettingsResponse
nodes.summary: A user's saved picks (client type `Settings`).

nodes.name: ApiException
nodes.summary: A refusal the client should show: an HTTP status and a message key ("auth.emailTaken") that the client translates into the user's language, plus, when the client needs more to act on it, a small data…

nodes.name: GlobalExceptionHandler
nodes.summary: Turns every failure into an ApiResponse, so a client never has to parse a second error format.

nodes.name: EmailService
nodes.summary: Renders a template and hands the letter to the SMTP server configured in `spring.mail.*`.

nodes.name: EmailTemplates
nodes.summary: The letter templates (location and names in EmailTemplateProperties), filled in by name: every {{key}} becomes its value, HTML-escaped.

nodes.name: Letter
nodes.summary: A rendered letter: the subject line and the HTML body.

nodes.name: VerificationCodeIssued
nodes.summary: A code was saved and its letter should go out.

nodes.name: VerificationMailListener
nodes.summary: Sends the confirmation letter once the code is safely in the database, on a thread of its own.

nodes.name: CodePurpose
nodes.summary: What a one-time code unlocks.

nodes.name: OneTimeCode
nodes.summary: A six-digit code sent by email, kept as a hash, good for a few guesses and a few minutes.

nodes.name: UserSettings
nodes.summary: A user's picks, the same on every device: look, language, the topic opened last.

nodes.name: RefreshToken
nodes.summary: One issued refresh token, by its SHA-256 only.

nodes.name: User
nodes.summary: An account.

nodes.name: JsonSecurityErrors
nodes.summary: 401 and 403 from the security filters, in the same ApiResponse shape as everything else.

nodes.name: JwtService
nodes.summary: Signs access tokens.

nodes.name: OneTimeCodes
nodes.summary: Six-digit codes for letters.

nodes.name: OpaqueTokens
nodes.summary: Refresh tokens: 256 random bits for the client, their SHA-256 for the database.

nodes.name: AuthWebService
nodes.summary: Sign-up with email confirmation, log in, refresh, log out.

nodes.name: AuthWebServiceImpl
nodes.summary: Each method is one transaction: rotation reads a locked row, revokes it and inserts its successor, and those must succeed or fail together.

nodes.name: SettingsWebService
nodes.summary: A user's picks kept on the server, so every device they sign in on starts the same: theme, accent, language, the topic opened last.
